sentences.text: 1 [2] The LA Collector collected certain sale deeds to determine the compensation but ultimately discarded all those  Page 2 of 13 deeds on the ground that location of those lands were not nearer to the acquired land and ultimately basing on the valuation chart, as maintained by the Government, assessed the valuation of the acquired land @Rs.4,00,000/- per kani.

An amount of Rs.3,22,400/- was also awarded by him as value of 403 numbers of rubber trees and further Rs.1000/- for 5 nos. of mango trees,
Rs.120/- for one karai tree, Rs.450/- for one Garjan tree and Rs.150/- for 2 nos. of Teak tree totalling Rs.3,24,120/-.
[3] The appellant insisted for reference under Section 18 of the LA Act before the LA Court and accordingly, after hearing, the LA Judge awarded compensation @Rs.6,00,000/- per kani.

The appellant was also allowed to receive compensation for 403 numbers of rubber trees @Rs.8,500/- for each tree, Rs.1,000/- for one koroi tree, Rs.1000/- for one garjan tree of diameter 2 inches and further Rs.1,000/- for two numbers of garjan trees of diameter 1 inch, Rs.1,500/- for five numbers of mango saplings and Rs.300/-
for two numbers of teak saplings, totalling Rs.34,30,300/-.
[4] This Court earlier in this appeal decided compensation for land @Rs.10,00,000/- per kani and the cost of each rubber tree @Rs.10,000/-.
Value of other trees as assessed by the LA Judge was, however, kept unaltered.

sentences.text: 2 [5] The appellant, thereafter, preferred Civil Appeal No.6280 of 2023 with SLP(C) No.15550 of 2022 and finally, the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 27.09.2023 remanded the matter for fresh determination of market value of the acquired land  Page 3 of 13 keeping in view of the exemplars relied upon by the appellant before the Land Acquisition Collector/Reference Court.

The relevant portion of observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is extracted herein below:
 "12.

It appears to us that the High Court ought not to  have determined the compensation only on the basis of  one sale instance or the amount claimed by the  appellants in their reference under Section 18 of the  Act.

All that the High Court was required to do was to  consider the sale instances and then determine as to  whether all the sale instances or any one of them is  comparable with the acquired land for the purpose of  assessing the fair and just market value of the acquired  land.

13 . For the reasons aforestated, the appeals are  allowed in part, the impugned judgments dated  16.07.2021 and 07.07.2021 are set aside and the  matters are remanded to the High Court for a fresh  determination of the market value of the acquired land  of the appellants keeping in view the exemplars relied  upon by them before the Land Acquisition  Collector/Reference Court.
14. It goes without saying that the High Court will  not reduce the compensation already awarded to the  appellants at the rate of Rs.10,00,000/- per kani.
15. We request the High Court to re-determine the  rate of compensation within a period of four months  from the date of appearance of the parties before the  High Court.
16. It is clarified that we have not expressed any  opinion on the merits of the appellant's claim.
17. As a result, the pending interlocutory  applications also stand disposed of."

In Mehrawal Khewaji Trust (Regd.) Faridkot & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Ors., 2012 AIR SCW 2822, at para-15, it was also observed by the Apex Court that when there are several exemplars with reference to similar lands (emphasis added), it is the general rule that the highest of the exemplars,

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When the land is being compulsorily taken away from a person, he is entitled to the highest value which similar land in the locality is shown to have fetched in a bona fide transaction entered into between a willing purchaser and a willing seller near about the time of the acquisition.

It was also observed that it would seem to be only fair that where the sale-deeds pertaining to different transactions are relied on behalf of the Government, the transaction representing the highest value should be preferred to the rest unless there are strong circumstances justifying a different course and it is not desirable to take an average of various sale- deeds placed before the authority/court for fixing fair compensation.
[15] The land under two sale deeds bearing no.1-1483 dated 19.11.2010 and bearing no.1-1535 dated 09.12.2010 are related to Bagan (tilla) class of land.
The distance of land under deed no.1- 1483 from acquired land is not discernible from the map and said land was transacted @ Rs.10 lakh per kani.
The land of deed no.1- 1535 is situated at a distance of 1.8 km from the acquired land and was transacted @ Rs.60,00,000/- per kani.
There is nothing in the evidence to suggest that said transaction was not a bona fide transaction.
However, as per the map under Ext.4/2, said land is situated at College Square area and much closer to the office of D.M. & Collector, South Tripura.
Hotel, Colleges, temples etc. are nearer to it.

The assessment note of the L.A. Collector also reflects this deed and also another sale deed where lands of bagan (tilla) class were sold @ Rs.60,00,000/-
per kani.
Therefore, transaction at such rate is not unusual in that mouja.

In light of the principle as laid in Mehrawal Khewaji Trust (Regd.) Faridkot & Ors. (Supra), deed no.1-1535 dated 09.12.2010 (Exbt.2 series) is taken into consideration subject to necessary deduction.
Said deed was executed for a very small tract of land of area 0.01 acre and it is situated just adjacent to Najrul market as constructed by Govt. of Tripura.
Therefore, it appears to be located in a commercial area.

Further,
the appellant in his cross-examination had admitted that the acquired land was situated at a distance of 2.5 Km from Belonia Municipal area.
30% deduction, therefore, is required to be made on that count considering higher potentiality of the land.
Considering the long distance between land of said deed and the acquired plot, 20% is deducted and considering small area of land sold under said sale exemplar, further 20% is deducted.
Thus, total deduction required to be made comes to (30%+20%+20%) =70%.
Market value of acquired land is, therefore, determined at (Rs.60,00,000 -70% of Rs.60,00,000)= Rs.18,00,000/- per kani.
No further benefit of escalation of price is given to the appellant.

The award passed by the L.A. Judge is completely bereft of reasoning,
and even there is no discussion of said deed no.1-1535 dated 09.12.2010 in the judgment.
The L.A.

Judge has mentioned some other sale exemplars in the judgment, going beyond the evidence.
[16] Learned Dy. S.G.I. though argued that the aerial distance of acquired plot from the sale exemplar could not be taken into consideration but such a plea was not convincing as the revenue map also demonstrates the distance measured by scale and not the physical distance based on road connectivity.
